Since the Renters' Rights Act requires two months' written notice unless the landlord agrees to less, the tenant's one-month notice isn't valid as given—so I need to calculate the earliest lawful departure date from the 10 Oct notice, which would be around 10 Dec 2026.

An earlier date like 10 Nov is only possible if the landlord explicitly agrees in writing, so that's really Ben's call, not mine. I should also flag the deposit process—it can only be returned after check-out and agreement on the final amount—and the need to coordinate key handover through the agency, then draft a reply to the tenant covering the correct notice period, the possibility of an earlier date pending landlord approval, and next steps on deposit and keys, while separately reaching out to Ben to get his written decision on the requested earlier end date.

This isn't a repair job, so no ticket is needed—just email the tenant and landlord directly and note the follow-up. I'll check the deposit amount against the weekly rent cap: £2,019 against roughly £403.80/week works out to about five weeks, which is within the legal limit, so no issue there. Let me send both messages now.

Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email, and congratulations on the new job in Manchester.

Since 1 May 2026, a tenant ending a tenancy needs to give at least two months' written notice. Your email received on 10 October 2026 is noted, but one month's notice is not enough on its own. The earliest date your tenancy can end from this notice is 10 December 2026.

If you'd like to leave on 10 November, we can ask your landlord, Ben Hartley, whether he will agree to a shorter period in writing. We can't promise he will, and we'll let you know his answer as soon as we have it. Until you hear from us in writing, please plan on the 10 December date.

Keys: once we have confirmed your end date, we'll arrange where and when to return them. Please don't post or leave keys anywhere until we've confirmed this with you.

Deposit: your deposit of £2,019 is held in the mydeposits scheme. We'll arrange its return once the tenancy has ended, the property has been checked out and the amount to be returned is agreed. Any dispute goes through the scheme's free dispute process.

Kind regards,
Lettings team
Mare & Co
